thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PD Alert fired: pd-emb-queue-high (policy: embeddings-queue-latency) -- urgent

pagerbot: Page details: incident#4521, severity: P1, service: embeddings-ingestion, region: us-west-2. Pager: sara-oncall. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incident/4521

sara-oncall: ack'd. I'm on it.

liam: oncall here, on standby if you need escalation. what metrics are spiking?

maya: seeing huge enqueue times and a backlog in the ingestion queue. dashboards show avg enqueue latency ~ 18s, backpressure rising.

sara-oncall: confirmed. customer-facing API errors have not spiked yet but batch ingestion throughput is dropping. rolling up logs now.

emily-sre: grabbing recent autoscaler events. quick look: 5xx on embedding-worker pods ~ 23:01 -> 23:03 and then CrashLoop for a subset.

jon: fyi i saw a similar blip earlier during a canary deploy this morning. could be a model variant with incompatible kv-cache.

maya: here's tail of the worker error: ```
2026-03-14T23:02:11Z ERROR worker-47: kv cache eviction mismatch: key not found
2026-03-14T23:02:12Z ERROR worker-47: out-of-memory allocating attention_buffer
```

liam: OOMs point to either memory regression in the image or a sudden request size change. any large batched jobs hitting now?

sara-oncall: checking recent user traces... one customer had a bulk upload (~120k records) at 22:59 UTC, which lines up. should we throttle ingestion or spin up extra workers?

emily-sre: autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough; policy has a min cooldown of 2m. we can force scale to mitigate. suggestion: scale deployment replicas to 24 (from 8) in us-west-2.

jon: +1 to force scale, but we should also isolate the canary model if present. guide: set routing weight for model v2-canary to 0 for ingestion route.

sara-oncall: executing now. running: `kubectl -n inference scale deploy embeddings-worker --replicas=24 --context=us-west-2`

incident-bot: Command logged by sara-oncall at 1739954380

maya: adjusting routing: `redwoodctl rollout set-weight --route ingestion-embeds --model v2-canary --weight 0`

pagerbot: :information_source: PagerDuty note appended by sara-oncall: "Scaling to 24 replicas and disabling v2-canary for ingestion route. Investigating OOMs. ETA unknown"

liam: after scale we should monitor queue length. dashboards -> embeddings.queue.length. also check per-pod mem usage.

emily-sre: pods coming up but a few still OOMing on startup; suspect container image change. listing recent images: v2-canary-image:sha=abc123, stable-image:sha=def456. Canary was pulled earlier today.

jon: if canary changed base runtime (new CUDA libs) that can cause kernel mismatches and memory regressions. rolling back canary was the right call.

sara-oncall: queue length trending down from 42k -> 9k after scale + weight change. partial recovery. ongoing: will keep an eye for customer errors.

customer-success-bot: Heads-up: CS alerted that two customers (acme-inc, studybox) reported delays in background ingestion jobs. CS will open support tickets if ETA > 30m.

maya: adding mitigation idea: enable prefix caching for known bulk uploader keys to reduce repeated recompute. low-risk toggle on the routing layer.

liam: do that after we confirm memory stabilizes. we don't want more churn.

sara-oncall: creating an incident ticket: RDW-4521, assigning runbook template "embeddings-high-queue". link: https://jira.example/browse/RDW-4521

emily-sre: note: I see one pod with repeated Java GC spikes and memory pressure. stack trace: ```
java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space
	at com.redwood.embed.Encoder.encode(Encoder.java:244)
```

jon: that's consistent with a model memory regression. let's pin ingestion to the stable-image and cordon any new nodes provisioned by the scale so they don't pull canary.

sara-oncall: pinning now: `kubectl set image deploy/embeddings-worker embeddings-worker=registry.redwood/stable-image:def456 -n inference`

incident-bot: Action logged by sara-oncall at 1739954425

maya: queue continuing to drain. errors metrics for request 5xx dropping from 150/min -> 8/min. good sign.

liam: can we get a rough ETA on full recovery?

sara-oncall: if OOMs don't reappear, and queue keeps draining at current rate, expect back to normal in ~20-30m. I'll escalate to emily if we see new OOMs.

customer-success-bot: Noted. CS has sent a templated message to impacted customers with "We're investigating ingestion delays; we will follow up shortly".

emily-sre: moving to postmortem ops: capture image hashes, autoscaler events, and full pod logs. tagging the incident for follow-up with research/infra.

jon: follow-up action: add a canary pre-check that runs a lightweight memory smoke test before enabling canary on ingestion route.

sara-oncall: agreed. adding to Jira RDW-4521 as action item.

liam: pinging infra on-call to consider reducing autoscaler cooldown for ingestion-worker pool — that would have helped here.

infra-oncall (not in channel): ACK and will propose tuning in the autoscaler policy doc.

sara-oncall: final status ping: queue drained to ~600, worker errors at baseline. moving incident to monitoring. keeping PD incident open for follow-up tasks.

pagerbot: :white_check_mark: Incident 4521 status set to "Mitigated - Monitoring". Logs and notes: https://pagerduty.example/incident/4521/notes

maya: :thumbsup: nice work team.

jon: adding retrospective owner assignment: emily-sre for infra/runbook changes; maya for caching playbook.

sara-oncall: signing off from primary. will be available on slack if anything regresses.

incident-bot: Thread closed by sara-oncall at 1739954498
